title: Teach every session to write the one document the new queue shows

decidedForYou.question: Do plans and launch prompts in a public repo get the writing checks?

options.label: No
options.consequence: A plan or a prompt is written for the session that runs it. READMEs, doc pages, pull requests, issues, and release notes in a public repo get the checks either way.

options.label: Yes
options.consequence: Every plan and prompt committed to a public repo goes through the standard, Vale, and `tellgrader` before it is committed. Ten repos are public, the workstation and the queue among them.

evidence.text: You said on 2026-11-12 that a file only a session reads can be written however works, and that the process also applies to items in public repos that might have human readers. Asked whether plans and launch prompts there get the checks, with "no" recommended, you answered "That's correct."

decidedForYou.question: Who checks a document before you see it?

options.label: A fresh reader with no context, in place of the separate writer
options.consequence: The session that did the work writes the document. A `sonnet` reader says what is being asked and what it couldn't follow, twice at most.

options.label: A separate writer drafts from a fact file, as today
options.consequence: This is the form you suspected of causing the stilted writing.

decidedForYou.applied: A fresh reader with no context, in place of the separate writer

decidedForYou.question: What happens if the new queue won't start at the switch?

options.label: The conductor reverts all four merges, pulls both repos, and tells you in chat
options.consequence: `restart` keeps the old server and the old state, so the old queue keeps working with the old skills.

options.consequence: The skills would describe a queue that isn't running.
